text: . CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, and Saurav Das, who were placed under preventive arrest yesterday, have been released by a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) Court in New Delhi today.According to the Delhi Police, all due legal procedures were followed, and the three individuals were produced before the SEM, Delhi Cantt this morning. The Police said that they were released upon furnishing a surety bond of 50 thousand rupees for maintaining peace and good behaviour for a period of one year.

. The United States has temporarily lifted sanctions on the sale and import of Russian-origin diesel fuel until 7th of April, 2027, following a conversation between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The US Treasury Department announced the decision last night, authorising transactions related to the sale, delivery, unloading and import of Russian diesel fuel, including imports into the United States.Diesel prices have surged globally amid disruptions to fuel supplies. Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries have affected production, prompting Moscow to impose restrictions on diesel exports. Attacks by Yemen’s Iran-backed armed group Houthi on facilities in Saudi Arabia have further tightened fuel supplies. The move comes as US President Donald Trump faces domestic political pressure to bring down fuel prices ahead of the US midterm elections in November.Speaking to media persons outside the White House, President Trump said Russia will immediately supply more than three lakh tonnes of diesel, followed by five lakh tonnes in November, one million tonnes thereafter and an additional three million tonnes, depending on the condition of Russian refineries.President Trump thanked the Russian President for agreeing to supply large quantities of diesel. He said the proposed supplies, along with what he described as US control of the Strait of Hormuz, would help bring down diesel prices. He described reducing fuel costs for American farmers, ranchers and truckers as his top priority.However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, meanwhile, warned that easing sanctions without a lasting agreement could allow Russia to prolong the war. He called for stronger sanctions, continued military support for Ukraine and increased pressure on Moscow to end the conflict.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh tomorrow. The districts that are likely to receive heavy rainfall include Rampur, Pilibhit, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Bahraich. Meanwhile, districts of Madhya Pradesh which are expected to receive rainfall include Satna, Chhatarpur, Tikamgarh and Niwari.IMD said that the line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya.The Met Department has also predicted heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim for the day. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty windsare expectedto prevail over Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of Northeast during the next two days.Meanwhile, parts of Delhi are expected to witness light to moderate rainfall tomorrow.

. Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana has completed one year today.  The scheme was launched on this day last year to strengthen agriculture in 100 Aspirational Agricultural Districts across the country. Our correspondent reports that the scheme has brought together 36 Central schemes across 11 Ministries and Departments, along with State schemes and private sector participation, to address district-specific agricultural needs.India’s agriculture sector has significant potential across diverse regions and farming communities. Approved by the Union Cabinet in July last year, the six-year initiative was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 11th October last year. It brings together 36 Central schemes across 11 Ministries and Departments, along with State schemes and private sector participation, to address district-specific agricultural needs. PMDDKY completed its first year, today marking a year of focused district-level action. Across 100 districts, District Action Plans and indicator-based monitoring are now in place. District-specific interventions are supporting agricultural development on the ground.The scheme aims to improve agricultural productivity, irrigation facilities, access to credit and post-harvest infrastructure. The Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana follows a three-tier implementation structure at the district, state and national levels. District Action Plans are prepared according to local agricultural needs, with progress monitored through one hundred twenty one indicators across 36 Central schemes.During the first year, all 100 selected districts prepared their action plans, which are under implementation. The average performance score of these districts increased from 18.85 in April 2026 to 46.89 in August 2026, reflecting improvement across all six objectives of the scheme. The initiative has also promoted knowledge-sharing among farmers. The PM-DDKY Farmer Producer Organisations Sangam, held in December 2025, brought together more than 72 Farmer Producer Organisations from 15 States and 33 scheme districts to share experiences and explore opportunities in agricultural productivity, market access and income enhancement. The progress achieved provides a foundation for stronger convergence and sustained agricultural development in the years ahead.

. Delhi Police has issued a traffic advisory for today in view of the law and order situation in the national capital. In its advisory, the traffic police said that diversions at different stretches will be enforced starting from 6 AM, depending upon the prevailing situation. It said that movement at various stretches, including Roundabouts of Shankar Road-Vande Matram ‘T’ Point towards New Delhi, Jhandewalan Panchkuian Marg, Gole Dak Khana and Patel Chowk and Mandi House, Bhairon Road-Ring Road T-Point and Lodhi Road Flyover, may be affected.It advised people to plan their journey in advance and avoid non-essential travel. The Traffic Police also said that traffic management measures are dynamic and will be relaxed or regulated based on real-time ground assessment. It also asked people to stay updated with real-time information.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Keralam, Mahe, Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal till tomorrow.Similar weather conditions are expected over Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Odisha and West Rajasthan during the same period. IMD also said that hot and humid weather conditions are likely at isolated places over Coastal Karnataka, Konkan and Goa today.

. In cricket, India will take on West Indies in the second of the five-match T20 International series in Ranchi today. The match will begin at 7 PM Indian Time.India led the series 1-0 after winning the opening match, with skipper Shreyas Iyer’s century powering the hosts to victory.

. In Badminton, two-time Olympic medallist P V Sindhu saw off Japan’s Riko Gunji to advance to the quarterfinals of women’s singles but it was curtains for the Indian men’s singles players at Arctic Open Super 500 tournament in Vantaa, Finland today. Sindhu, who won the Japan Open Super 750 title in July, notched up a 21-15 21-15 win over Gunji in the second round. The sixth-seeded Indian will now face top seed and former world champion Ratchanok Inthanon from Thailand.However, it was a disappointing outing for Tharun Mannepalli and Tanvi Sharma, who suffered straight-game defeats. Second seed Christo Popov of France beat Mannepalli 21-14, 21-19, while Ratchanok defeated Tanvi 21-18, 21-7. Kidambi Srikanth also bowed out in the opening round after losing 21-15, 15-21, 13-21 to Canada’s Brian Yang.Later in the day, men’s doubles pair of Krishna Prasad Garaga and Pruthvi Krishnamurthy Roy will face England’s Oliver Butler and Samuel Jones.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over coastal and South Interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry for the next 2-3 days. The IMD said thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds may prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura tomorrow. Meanwhile, Konkan and Goa may experience Hot and Humid weather tomorrow.

. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has registered a case to investigate last month’s mid-air cockpit attack on Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight. The case has been registered under the relevant provisions of the Anti-Hijacking Act, 2016, and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.Captain Machchhar, who hails from Gujarat, was stabbed and seriously injured by his co-pilot in the cockpit of flydubai flight while travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv on 30th of last month. The flight was carrying 174 passengers, including 27 children. Several leaders across the world praised the bravery of Captain Machchhar who saved the lives of passengers despite being injured.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has removed Paytm Payments Bank Ltd (PPBL) from the list of scheduled banks following the cancellation of its banking licence. The RBI said PPBL has been excluded from the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. The notification was published on July 31 and later notified in the Gazette of India.The central bank had cancelled PPBL’s banking licence in April for non-compliance with regulatory norms, stating that the bank’s affairs were being conducted in a manner detrimental to the interests of depositors.The Delhi High Court subsequently ordered the winding up of Paytm Payments Bank.PPBL has faced several regulatory restrictions in recent years. In March 2022, the RBI barred the bank from onboarding new customers following supervisory concerns. Further restrictions were imposed in January and February 2024, including a ban on accepting fresh deposits, credits and top-ups in customer accounts, prepaid instruments and wallets.

. The 57th GST Council meeting is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman is chairing the meeting. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Karnataka Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, and Finance Ministers of States and Union Territories are also attending the meeting.The GST Council meeting will discuss policy reforms to resolve GST disputes and improve the flow of input tax credit, with the aim of reducing the time and cost of compliance. Sources in the Finance Ministry said that the government will propose a five-pronged plan for the next set of reforms to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) system. These reforms are aimed at automating and easing many of the current administrative bottlenecks in the GST system and reducing the compliance burden, especially for small businesses.The five-pronged proposal covers process reforms, structural reforms, ease of living and doing business, exports of services, and e-commerce. Some of the key changes proposed involve automatic invoice matching between buyers and sellers, reducing paperwork around claiming input tax credits (ITC), reducing the number of times small taxpayers have to file returns, and removing multi-state registrations for small businesses.The last, 56th meeting of the GST Council was held in September last year. During the meeting, the Council approved rate rationalisation with a focus on the common man, labour-intensive industries, farmers and agriculture, health, and key drivers of the economy.

. GST Council has removed power of arrest of tax officers and the Council has raised the threshold for prosecution from one crore rupees to 5 crore rupees. The punishment, whether fine or imprisonment or both, has been left to judicial discretion in every case. A taxpayer who files late, makes a mistake or falls behind on payment will face recovery, interest and a proportionate penalty.Addressing media following GST Council meeting in New Delhi this evening, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said no rate changes has been made in GST Council meeting and the rate structure is settled. She said that GST Council today has recommended common standards for notices and proceedings and no notices below the prescribed monetary threshold of ten thousand rupees, including withdrawal of pending notices below the said threshold. She said notices will not be issued for monetary thresholds of 10,000 rupees or below.

. India T20I captain Shreyas Iyer has climbed to a career-best seventh spot in the latest ICC rankings for the shortest format, while ODI skipper Shubman Gill has retained the top position in the ODI format.Shreyas Iyer climbed 18 places to a career-best seventh in the ICC T20I batting rankings after scoring an unbeaten 102 off 43 balls, making him India’s third-highest-ranked batter in the format. Ishan Kishan and Abhishek Sharma remain in the top two, while Tilak Varma is in 10th position.Axar Patel rose 16 places to seventh among T20I bowlers after taking six wickets in three matches.In ODIs, Shubman Gill retained the top spot after scoring an unbeaten 223 against the West Indies, reaching a career-best 841 rating points. Virat Kohli slipped to third, while KL Rahul jumped seven places to 10th position after scoring a swashbuckling hundred in the third ODI against the West Indies.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate projects worth 13,000 crore rupees in Chennai, Tamil Nadu today. Prime Minister will flag off the metro rail service of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around 4900 crore rupees. Mr Modi will also undertake a ride on the Chennai Metro from Porur Bypass Station to Poonamallee Bypass Station and back.The Poonamallee – Porur corridor features a unique 3.7-km double-decker structure with advanced signalling systems designed to support driverless operations. The Prime Minister will dedicate and inaugurate railway infrastructure projects worth over 750 crore rupees, including five Amrit Stations at Palani, Vellore Cantonment, Ambasamudram, Paramakudi and Namakkal, which have been redeveloped under the Amrit Bharat Station scheme. Mr Modi will perform Darshan and Pooja at the Jalakandeswarar Temple near the Porur lake.The stage is all set for the Prime Minister’s visit today at Chennai. The city has brightened up to welcome the Prime Minister as he is set to launch several projects based on infrastructure in road development , ports and innovation in sciences. This includes laying  the foundation stone and inauguration of  key National Highway projects to strengthen maritime infrastructure, expand cargo-handling capacity and improve logistics efficiency.The road projects will reduce the travel time apart from easing traffic congestion in National Highways in Salem, Madurai and Nagapattinam. He will also lay the foundation stone for  Lube Oil Base Stocks project at the existing Manali Refinery of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited.The prime minister will also inaugurate an additional Coal Berth project and lay the foundation stone for capital dredging works for additional  Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port . Mr Modi will dedicate to the nation the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras, a  pioneering global scientific mission to map more than 100 human brains into three-dimensional atlases at cellular resolution, across the human lifespan – from the foetal stage to old age. Prime Minister will participate in the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya School in Chennai before leaving to Delhi.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, South Interior Karnataka and Uttarakhand tomorrow. It has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over North Eastern parts of India, including Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, during the next two days. According to IMD, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Odisha and Telangana are also likely to witness similar weather conditions tomorrow.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices rebounded today. The Sensex advanced 879 points, or 1.23 per cent to close at 72,472. The Nifty gained 289 points, or 1.3 per cent to settle at 22,520.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index rose nearly 1.7% and the Smallcap 100 index added over half a per cent.

. Estonia has invited Indian IT professionals and technology companies to explore business opportunities in Europe through its e-residency programme, with the country’s Minister of Justice and Digital Affairs, Liisa Pakosta, saying that Indian talent is warmly welcome.Her remarks came amid the US government’s suspension of certain major technology and IT outsourcing firms from the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme.Speaking to the media on the sidelines of the India Mobile Congress in New Delhi today, Pakosta highlighted Estonia’s e-residency initiative, which enables entrepreneurs to establish and manage companies in the European Union digitally without having to relocate physically to Estonia.She said there was considerable scope for Indian and Estonian businesses to collaborate, invest in each other’s markets and expand innovative products and services.Pakosta added that the proposed India-European Union Free Trade Agreement could further enhance cooperation, particularly in the digital services sector.The Estonian minister also praised India’s technological expertise and strong research and development ecosystem, expressing her country’s interest in partnering with Indian companies and professionals to develop innovative solutions.She identified cybersecurity and digital public infrastructure as key areas for future collaboration, particularly as artificial intelligence-driven threats continue to grow more sophisticated.Pakosta said Estonia was keen to leverage India’s research and development capabilities to address emerging cybersecurity challenges and strengthen technological cooperation between the two countries.

. Paralympic champions Pramod Bhagat and Bhavina Patel will lead the Indian contingent as flag bearers at the Opening Ceremony of the Asian Para Games, which will get underway later this month. The Games will be held from 18th to 24th October at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan, with athletes from across Asia competing in the grand sporting event. Para badminton star Pramod Bhagat has won six Asian Para Games medals, including two gold and four bronze, between 2014 and 2023. Para table tennis player Bhavina Patel has also won two Asian Para Games medals – a silver and a bronze – between 2018 and 2023.Calling it a proud moment, Ms Patel said carrying the Tricolour means representing something much bigger than oneself.The Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) will formally see off the Indian contingent at a special ceremony tomorrow. Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya will attend the event as Chief Guest, with Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Nikhil Khadse as Guest of Honour.PCI President Devendra Jhajharia said Bhagat and Patel are exceptional champions whose achievements and resilience make them fitting representatives of the Indian contingent.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

. Northern Railway has announced that all train services will operate as per their normal schedule today. Railways had decided to cancel Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4 am and 2 pm yesterday.

. In Badminton, Indian Men’s Doubles pair Krishna Prasad Garaga and Pruthvi Krishnamurthy Roy advanced to the second round of the Arctic Open Super 500 tournament at Vantaa in Finland, today.The Indian duo produced a stunning upset, defeating fifth seeds He Ji Ting and Ren Xiang Yu of China 10-21, 21-18, 22-20 in a closely fought opening-round match.However, in Men’s Singles, HS Prannoy suffered an early exit, losing 10-21, 9-21 to fourth-seeded Dane Anders Antonsen.In Women’s Singles, two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu advanced to the pre-quarterfinals after defeating Canada’s Wen Yu Zhang 21-8, 21-11.Tanvi Sharma also progressed to the second round, beating Taiwan’s Chiu Pin Chian 21-15, 21-17. However, Isharani Baruah went down 10-21, 15-21 to top seed Ratchanok Intanon of Thailand.Unnati Hooda, Ashmita Chaliha and Malvika Bansod also bowed out in the opening rounds. Unnati lost to China’s Han Qian Xi, while Ashmita was beaten by Denmark’s Line Christophersen in a tight three-game contest. Malvika went down to Scotland’s Kirsty Gilmour in straight games.

. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas conducted a special inspection drive in Delhi to assess road dust and effectiveness of road cleaning operations across the city.The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has informed that the commission deployed four flying squad teams for the inspection which was carried out yesterday. The Flying Squad Teams inspected 25 road stretches covering approximately 35 kilometres of the Inner and Outer ring road which come under the jurisdiction of the Public Works Department (PWD), Delhi.The Ministry highlighted that the inspections, which were meant to seek strict implementation of road cleaning and dust mitigation measures, found 17 cases of violation. These violations include accumulation of construction and demolition waste and high visible road dust across inspected road stretches.CAQM has directed PWD, Delhi and other concerned agencies to take appropriate corrective measures to control road dust on priority basis. It also added the inspection shall continue under Operation Clean Air across Delhi-NCR to assess on-ground implementation of various air pollution abatement measures.

. Union Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting Dr L Murugan met with Indian para-swimmer and sporting icon, Padma Shri awardee Satendra Singh Lohiya. In a social media post, Mr Murugan said that Satendra Singh’s inspiring journey of courage, perseverance and sporting excellence continues to motivate and inspire millions across the nation.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today paid tributes to Maharaja Agrasen on his birth anniversary. In a social media post, Mr Modi highlighted that Maharaja Agrasen was a pioneer of public service and social harmony, whose life and ideals continuously guide society towards humanity. The Prime Minister added that his great thoughts will forever inspire India’s cultural resurgence.Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh also paid tributes to freedom fighter Loknayak Jayaprakash Narayan on his birth anniversary. In a post on social media, Mr Shah said Jayaprakash Narayan’s entire life was dedicated to the nation and society, from mobilising youth power in the freedom struggle to empowering rural India and working for Sarvodaya after Independence. He said the Loknayak’s dedication will continue to guide future generations.The Defence Minister said Jayaprakash Narayan’s life is a symbol of unwavering commitment to democratic values and the national interest. He said the call for ‘Sampoorn Kranti’ was a resolve for integrity in politics, accountability in governance and moral rejuvenation in society.The Defence Minister noted that during the dark chapter of the Emergency, the Loknayak opposed dictatorship with indomitable courage. The Minister added that his struggle to protect the Constitution, civil liberties and democratic rights will forever remain memorable in Indian history.

. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar chaired a conference of India’s Heads of Mission in Africa in Addis Ababa yesterday. Speaking on the occasion, he said, India and Africa share deep linkages built upon Global South solidarity, strategic autonomy, multipolarity and common development aspirations.The conference came a day after Dr Jaishankar laid out his vision for the India-Africa partnership in an address in the Ethiopian capital. On Friday, the minister said partnerships of the future must help create capabilities, not promote dependencies, and called for a reformed UN Security Council with fair representation for Africa, while speaking on the India-Africa partnership at the Adwa Memorial Museum in Addis Ababa.

. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has said that under the ongoing 100-week Sankalp Abhiyan, initiatives like MY BHARAT and the National Service Scheme mentored more than 1.06 Lakh participants against substance abuse from across 200 designated institutions and adopted villages.The Ministry highlighted that moving ahead from conventional pledge taking activities, the Yuva Samwad Mela emphasised interactive dialogue, public awareness and cultural expression to encourage informed conversations on the harmful effects of substance abuse.The Ministry, which concluded the first Month of Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan, underscored that the nationwide initiative includes three major components, including youth dialogue, awareness stalls and cultural performances. It also noted that with the completion of its first month, the second month will focus on physical fitness and sports under the theme ‘Fit Youth, Addiction-Free Youth’.

. US President Donald Trump has suggested that Ukraine should elect a new president capable of negotiating a deal to end the conflict with Russia. He also warned Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy against targeting Russian oil refineries, particularly those producing diesel fuel.Speaking on the White House premises, Trump argued that such strikes could disrupt fuel supplies to global markets and adversely affect American farmers and ranchers. His remarks came a day after he announced on Truth Social that Russia would immediately supply more than 3 lakh tonnes of diesel fuel to American and global markets, with additional shipments expected in the coming months.

. In Men’s Cricket, the West Indies defeated India by six wickets in the second T20 International in Ranchi last night, levelling the five-match series to 1-1.Chasing a target of 250 runs, West Indies overhauled the score, posting 252 runs for the loss of four wickets in 18.3 overs, winning the match with nine balls to spare. Captain Shai Hope led from the front with a magnificent 102 off 45 balls, while Sherfane Rutherford’s 84 off 37 set the chase alight.Earlier, put in to bat, India posted a formidable total of 249 for five in stipulated 20 overs. Sanju Samson top-scored for India with a brilliant 82 off 41 balls. Ishan Kishan with 43 off 22 balls also made a valuable contribution. Hope was adjudged Player of the Match for his outstanding performance. The third T20 International between India and West Indies will be played in Indore tomorrow. The match is scheduled to begin at 7 PM.

. India’s Putul Sonowal has created history by assuring the country’s first-ever medal at the World Bowls Champion of Champions in Barham, Australia. The 43-year-old from Assam achieved the milestone by reaching the semi-finals of the men’s singles event. Sonowal defeated Singapore’s Harriman Yuen in the quarter-finals to secure his place in the last four.A member of the Assam Police, Sonowal has emerged as one of India’s leading lawn bowls players. He won the Men’s Singles gold medal at the 2026 Asian Lawn Bowls Championship, further strengthening his standing on the international stage. Earlier, at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Sonowal defeated Canada’s Ryan Bester, a three-time Commonwealth Games medallist and former world outdoor champion, in the Men’s Singles event. The match went to a tie-break after both players won one set each, with Sonowal emerging victorious.

. Today is World Cotton Day. This day is celebrated annually on October 7 to highlight the global economic, social, and environmental importance of cotton. The theme for this year is Cotton for Good: Building Prosperity Through Trade, Transformation and Partnership. Sharing a video message, Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh extended greetings to everyone associated with this sector.He said that this day honours farmers who cultivate cotton in the fields, thereby enabling employment for workers across the entire value chain, whether in spinning mills, ginneries, textile manufacturing units, or garment factories. He informed that 60 lakh farmers in the country are engaged in cotton cultivation. He underlined that countless small enterprises are linked to the handloom industries that not only operate domestically but also export their products.

. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan has extended greetings to the citizens on the occasion of Navratri today. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan expressed hope that Goddess Durga’s blessings bestow strength, courage, and sound wisdom upon everyone. He also expressed hope that with the grace of Goddess Jagadamba, the Government shall fulfil the resolve to build a strong, prosperous, and developed India.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also extended his greetings to the people on the commencement of Navratri today. In a social media post, Mr Modi offered his prayers to Maa Shailaputri. In his post, the Prime Minister also shared a video of a Tamil devotional song, Karpoora Nayagiye. Mr Modi expressed hope that the blessings of the Goddess will inspire patience and self-confidence among the people. He also wished that the divine blessings of Maa will always remain upon the people of the country.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today paid tribute to Loknayak Jayaprakash Narayan on his birth anniversary. In a social media post, the Prime Minister said that his appeal transcended generations and inspired people to view public life as an instrument of national renewal. He also recalled Jayaprakash Narayan’s fearless voice during the Emergency.Mr Modi said that Loknayak JP was deeply committed to good governance and the welfare of the marginalised sections of society. The Prime Minister reaffirmed the government’s commitment to upholding his ideals while working towards building a Viksit Bharat.

. Three Saudi nationals were killed and several others injured in attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh yesterday, Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said. The attacks targeted airport facilities and a Saudia Airlines aircraft, causing material damage. Saudia stated that no passengers were aboard the aircraft but said Captain Hamoud Ali Alkalthami, a member of its staff, was killed.The Saudi-led coalition said it had destroyed three rocket launch platforms used by the Houthis and warned that attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure would be met with a firm response. Meanwhile, Houthi-run Al Masirah TV reported air strikes on sites in Sana’a and Saada, including telecommunications facilities.Meanwhile, the US Embassy in the UAE has urged American citizens to exercise heightened vigilance amid the regional security situation in the region, warning of possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly, it added.

. The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

. Delhi Metro Rail Corporation has informed that the entry and exit gates of all 45 metro stations, which were closed due to security reasons, are now open. It added that interchange facilities at all the concerned Metro stations are also available. Delhi Metro had closed 45 metro stations till 10 PM yesterday due to security reasons.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has introduced a ‘Credit Risk-o-Meter’ as a mandatory disclosure mechanism to help investors assess the credit risk of debt securities before investing. The colour-coded risk indicator will have to be displayed in offer documents, abridged prospectuses, private placement memorandums and advertisements issued by issuers and online bond platform providers (OBPPs). It will also be required on OBPP web and mobile platforms.SEBI said the measure aims to provide investors with a clear visual representation of credit risk and support informed investment decisions.The new provisions will come into effect 45 days from the date of the circular. Stock exchanges and depositories have been directed to put in place the necessary systems and processes for implementation.

India has said that the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) ’s concerns regarding yesterday’s events in Delhi are misplaced and constitute an unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of the country.In a statement, the Permanent Mission of India in Geneva said that OHCHR should also devote attention to large-scale protests elsewhere, consistent with its mandate of impartiality and non-selectivity. It highlighted that India is the world’s largest democracy, where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by the Constitution and safeguarded by robust institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media.It stressed that, as in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order. It added that the authorities act in accordance with the law, and courts remain available to all for redressal of any grievances.

In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. The second India- European Free Trade Association (EFTA) Prosperity Summit was held in New Delhi today. The summit brought together senior Indian and EFTA officials, business leaders and industry representatives to discuss trade, investment and economic cooperation. President of Switzerland Guy Parmelin who is currently on a three day visit to India was present in the Summit. He arrived in New Delhi on Monday. India and the  EFTA, comprising Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, mark one year since the implementation of their Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement.Talking to reporters after attending the Summit, Information and Broadcasting Minister  Ashwini Vaishnaw said that  productive discussions took place  between the Ministers and businesses on both sides.Mr Vaishnaw said that the European countries today considers  India as a major hub for innovation and manufacturing. He said, several kinds of partnerships are being established with India, which will also facilitate the exchange of technology. He said, this is expected to create approximately one million new jobs in total and generate new opportunities for the youth.

. The United Arab Emirates’ investigation into the flydubai flight FZ1073 incident has uncovered a premeditated terrorist plot by the aircraft’s Omani co-pilot. UAE Attorney-General Counsellor Dr Hamad Saif Al Shamsi yesterday announced further details of the Public Prosecution’s investigation into the incident.The Attorney-General said the 29-year-old suspect had planned to seize control of the aircraft and use it to carry out a suicide attack on the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, with the aim of causing the maximum possible loss of life. Investigators found that the suspect had taken two previous flights to Tel Aviv to familiarise himself with the route and the airport. These trips were allegedly part of his preparations for the plot, which he began attempting to execute during his third flight to Tel Aviv on 30th September.On the day of the incident, the suspect allegedly caught the captain by surprise inside the cockpit and attacked him with an emergency axe. The captain resisted the assault and attempted to call for help. A pilot assigned to the return flight was also on board and happened to be near the cockpit when the attack occurred. He noticed the cockpit door opening and closing repeatedly in an unusual manner, which aroused his suspicions. He approached the cockpit and attempted to enter using the access code. After gaining entry, he witnessed the suspect attacking the captain.The pilot immediately intervened with the assistance of a cabin crew member and several passengers. Together, they rescued the injured captain and restrained the suspect. The captain and co-pilot assigned to the return flight subsequently regained control of the aircraft, diverted it and landed safely at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia.The investigation found that the suspect’s alleged radicalisation began in 2017, while he was studying in Australia. He was reportedly influenced by extremist literature and online content promoting terrorist organisations and suicide attacks, which led him to adopt violent extremist beliefs. According to the findings, the suspect was also inspired by the September 11 attacks in the United States. In his confession, he reportedly linked his decision to pursue a career in aviation to his intention to carry out a similar attack.The Emirates News Agency (WAM) reported that the suspect gave a detailed confession in the presence of his lawyer, with all legally prescribed safeguards in place. His confession reportedly outlined his motives and the various stages of planning and attempting to execute the alleged plot.The UAE Public Prosecution has also recorded statements from the aircraft’s captain, the pilot assigned to the return flight, his co-pilot and other crew members. The investigation is ongoing, with the Public Prosecution continuing to examine the evidence, review recordings and technical reports, and investigate possible accomplices or other connections to the alleged plot.

Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey today called for greater participation of women in financial decision-making and investment.Addressing the AMFI-Pinkathon Investor Awareness Programme during World Investor Week 2026, Pandey said financial independence meant not only earning but also having the knowledge and confidence to make informed financial decisions. He said women account for around 25 per cent of capital market participation and 27 per cent of individual mutual fund investors.There are now more than 1.6 crore women mutual fund investors in India. Pandey highlighted SEBI’s Project Jagrook, aimed at expanding investor education through multiple platforms and languages. He said its WhatsApp campaign had delivered over 24 crore messages in three days. He urged women to take small, informed and consistent steps towards financial well-being.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said that banks will need to maintain 99 per cent of the required cash reserve ratio (CRR) daily starting from October 16, up from 90 per cent at present. The move follows a review of the current liquidity condition in the banking system and will help reduce the banking system liquidity, which stood at a surplus of around 3.88 lakh crore rupees as of October 8.

. India has strongly rejected the remarks made by the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) regarding recent events in New Delhi, terming them unwarranted and an unacceptable interference in the country’s internal affairs.In a statement, the Ministry of External Affairs emphasised that as the world’s largest democracy, India guarantees the right to peaceful assembly under its Constitution, backed by robust institutions, an independent judiciary, and a free media. It noted that, like any democracy, these rights are exercised subject to public order and safety, with law enforcement authorities acting strictly according to the law and legal avenues available to all.India also highlighted the OHCHR’s selective approach, pointing out that violent responses to protests in India’s neighbourhood and law enforcement actions in the UN body’s own vicinity have gone uncommented. New Delhi cautioned that such double standards seriously erode the credibility of multilateral institutions.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices extended losses today amid weak global cues. The Sensex tanked 1,045 points, or 1.44 per cent to close at 71,593. The Nifty dropped 371 points, or 1.64 per cent to settle at 22,232.The broader market at the National Stock Exchange ended with deeper cuts. The Midcap 100 index lost over 2.5 per cent and the Smallcap 100 index declined more than 2.3 per cent.In the Sensex pack, 27 of the 30 constituent companies logged losses. Among the top underperformers, ITC shed over 4.2 per cent, Indigo dropped nearly 3.4 per cent and PowerGrid fell almost 3.2 per cent. In contrast, Tech Mahindra rose over 0.4 per cent, and Axis Bank as well as Infosys added over 0.2 per cent each.All 28 sectoral indices on the BSE succumbed to selling pressure. Among the top laggards, Power plunged 3.5 per cent, Utilities fell 3.4 per cent, and Metal dropped more than 3.3 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 3,426 companies declined, 1,003 advanced and 225 remained unchanged.

. Russian strikes killed at least 11 people and injured 16 others in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, officials said today, a day after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel. Mykhailo Semikin, the head of the regional military administration, alleged that Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia. Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4.5 years since Moscow’s military operation.The latest attacks came a day after Mr. Trump said he had struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a stunning reversal of years of US pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the US midterm elections.In a social media post, Mr. Trump said that he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call. Reacting to the deal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, it help bankroll Moscow’s war in Ukraine. Mr. Trump announced the deal as his envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were meeting with Ukrainian officials in Miami to discuss a proposal to end the war.

. India’s live events sector grew by 44 per cent over the last one year, with around 34 thousand events held across the country. Secretary of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Chanchal Kumar said this, addressing the 5th meeting of the Live Events Development Cell in New Delhi today. He said that the sector is now supporting more than one crore livelihoods. The Secretary also said the Government has set an ambitious target of doubling the sector by 2030, with the potential to generate 15-20 million direct and ancillary jobs.The meeting reviewed the implementation of the Single Window Clearances Portal for the live event industry on the India Cine Hub (ICH) portal. States and UTs were asked to designate Nodal Officers, nominate authorised officers from departments, integrate departmental and local licensing systems with the ICH Portal, route the complete licence lifecycle through the portal, onboard live event venues and notify live event licensing as a time-bound public service.

In Table Tennis, Indian paddlers Manush Shah and Diya Chitale created history by becoming the first Indian mixed doubles pair to reach the semifinals of a WTT Grand Smash after beating Romania’s Eduard Ionescu and Bernadette Szocs 3-0 at the China Smash in Beijing yesterday.The fifth-seeded Indian duo won the quarterfinal 11-9, 13-11, 11-3 to secure a place in the last four.However, Manav Thakkar exited the men’s singles in the round of 32 after losing 0-3 to seventh seed Alexis Lebrun of France.In women’s doubles, Diya Chitale and Yashaswini Ghorpade suffered a narrow 2-3 defeat to China’s Gao Yuxin and Xiang Junlin in the round of 16.

. Mahalaya, marking the advent of Goddess Durga, is being observed today with religious rituals and devotional programmes by Hindu communities across Bangladesh. The occasion signifies the end of Pitru Paksha, dedicated to ancestors, and the beginning of Devi Paksha, the auspicious fortnight preceding Durga Puja.Dhakeshwari National Temple in Dhaka is organising a special programme, including prayers and til-tarpan offerings for the departed souls of ancestors. Ramna Kali Mandir is also holding Mahalaya celebrations. Indian High Commissioner in Bangladesh Sh. Dinesh Trivedi attended the ceremony.Devotees mark the occasion by offering prayers and listening to the recitation of the Sree Sree Chandi. The traditional Mahishasura Mardini programme. Mahalaya signals the beginning of the countdown to Durga Puja, the largest religious festival of Bangladesh’s Hindu community. The five-day festival will formally begin with Maha Shashthi on October 16 and conclude with the immersion of idols on Bijoya Dashami on October 21.
